title: The Silent Space Mystery
text: Imagine floating in space. Two astronauts are outside their spaceship, right next to each other. One of them screams as loud as possible. The other hears... absolutely nothing. Why?

title: Think About It
text: When you speak on Earth, what exactly is moving from your mouth to someone else's ear? Is something physical leaving your body, or is it something else entirely?

content.title: The Domino Effect of Sound
content.description: Just like falling dominoes push the next one without moving across the room, particles in the air bump into each other to pass the sound energy forward.

title: What is Sound?
text: Sound is a form of energy that produces a sensation of hearing in our ears. It travels as a mechanical wave, which means it requires a material medium (like air, water, or steel) to propagate. This is why astronauts can't hear each other in space—there is no air to carry the wave!

content.definition: A wave that requires a physical medium to travel through.

question: Which of the following environments would not allow sound to travel?
options: Inside a solid block of iron
In the vacuum of outer space

content.title: Reflection: Feel the Vibration
content.text: Place your hand gently on your throat and say 'Ahhhh' loudly. Now whisper it. What difference do you feel in your fingers? Can you explain why based on what we've learned?

content.title: Connection to Energy
content.text: Remember our previous chapter on Energy? When you hit a drum, your kinetic energy is transferred to the drum skin, which vibrates and transfers that energy to the air molecules. Sound is simply moving energy!

content.title: Mastery Challenge & Common Trap
content.text: Make a string telephone with two paper cups and a tight string. Why does it work? A common mistake is thinking air particles travel from your mouth to the other person's ear. They don't! The string passes the vibration energy forward much better than air.
